cjr.quadtree.spec.model.build_tree_corre.description: The lemma states that if rectangle b has side length width d and every point in xs lies inside b (including its lower boundaries but excluding its upper boundaries), then build_tree d b xs produces a valid quadtree whose contents are exactly the set of points in xs, ignoring duplicates and order. Validity means leaves lie in their assigned rectangles and branches occur only at positive depth, with valid children in the four quadrants. The supplied unit_unique lemma explains why keeping only the first point at depth zero preserves the set: all points in such a square are equal. The definition of width is not supplied, so its numerical relationship to depth is unspecified.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.child_box.description: child_box takes a natural number d, a rectangle b with integer coordinates, and a quadrant, and constructs the corresponding lower-left, lower-right, upper-left, or upper-right rectangle using b’s outer bounds and split coordinates xmin b + width d and ymin b + width d. No premises constrain these coordinates; since width is not defined in the input, it is not established that the splits are actual midpoints or that the resulting rectangles lie within b.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.child_route.description: The lemma states that if b is a square with side length 2^(d+1) and p lies inside it, then p also lies inside the child rectangle selected by route, which compares p’s coordinates with the square’s horizontal and vertical midpoints. Rectangle membership includes the lower bounds and excludes the upper bounds, so points exactly on a dividing line are routed to the right or upper child.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.child_route_uniq.description: The lemma states that if point p lies in the child rectangle for quadrant k of rectangle b, then route d b p returns k. Membership includes the rectangle’s lower bounds and excludes its upper bounds. The child rectangles and routing function use the same split coordinates, xmin b + 2^d and ymin b + 2^d; points exactly on a split are routed right or up. Membership in the chosen child rectangle is the only stated premise, and no proof is supplied.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.child_square.description: The lemma states that if rectangle b has both coordinate spans equal to width(d + 1), then any quadrant k selected by child_box has both spans equal to width(d). The child boundaries use the parent’s edges and split points xmin(b) + width(d) and ymin(b) + width(d); the supplied width_succ lemma states that width(d + 1) is twice width(d). No additional premise restricts the quadrant, and the input provides no proof of the lemma.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.child_subset.description: The lemma states that if b is a square with side length width (d + 1), then any point p inside its selected child quadrant k is also inside b. The child rectangles split b at coordinates width d above its lower bounds; the supplied width relation makes this half the parent’s side length. Rectangle membership includes the lower boundaries and excludes the upper boundaries.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.children_enumera.description: The lemma states that two quadtrees valid at depth d in different child quadrants of the same square b cannot enumerate a common point. It assumes b has width and height width(S d), the quadrant indices k and j differ, and each tree is valid in its corresponding child box; assuming a point p appears in both enumerations then yields a contradiction. Enumeration collects leaf points, while validity requires leaves to lie in their assigned rectangles and branches to respect the depth and subdivision. The supplied declarations state that distinct child boxes are disjoint, although the exact boundary convention for rectangle membership is not given.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.contains_set.description: contains_set takes a point p, represented as a pair of integers, and a finite set S of such points, and returns a Boolean indicating whether p belongs to S: true if it does, and false otherwise.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.contains_state.description: contains_state takes a point p and a quadtree t and returns a pair containing the original tree t and a Boolean indicating whether p belongs to its contents. The contents are the empty set for Empty, the singleton point set for a Leaf, and the union of the four child trees’ contents for a Branch. This is a definition, not a correctness or termination contract.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.contains_state_r.description: The lemma states that applying contains_state twice with the same p, passing the state returned by the first call into the second, yields the original state t and equal answers a and b. The supplied definition returns its input state unchanged together with contains_set p (contents t), which explains both equalities. No additional premises are stated; the input does not define contains_set or contents, so their precise interpretation is not established.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.contents.description: The recursive function contents collects the set of points in a quadtree: an Empty tree gives the empty set, a Leaf p gives the singleton set containing p, and a Branch gives the union of the sets collected from its four subtrees. Its result has type points, defined as gset point, so repeated occurrences of a point do not produce duplicate set entries.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.coordinate_int64.description: The lemma states that if the natural-number depth d is at most 30 and point p lies in domain d, then both coordinates of p are within the signed 64-bit integer range, from -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807 inclusive. The domain is defined as Rect 0 0 (width d) (width d), and membership requires each coordinate to be at least its rectangle’s minimum and strictly below its maximum; the supplied width_bound lemma states that width d is at most 1073741824 under the same depth assumption. No proof is supplied, so this describes the claim without asserting verification.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.domain.description: For a natural number d, domain d constructs a rectangle whose minimum x and y coordinates are both 0 and whose maximum x and y coordinates are both 2 raised to the power d, stored as integers. This gives the bounds of a square, but the supplied definitions do not specify whether its boundary points are included.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.enumerate.description: The recursive function enumerate takes a quadtree and returns a list of its leaf points, each a pair of integers. An empty tree contributes no points, a leaf contributes its single point, and a branch concatenates the lists from its four children in their declared order: ll, lr, ul, ur. It recurses on child trees, preserves repeated points, and requires no additional premises; the input does not specify geometric constraints on the tree.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.enumerate_conten.description: For every quadtree t, this lemma states that converting the list produced by enumerate t into a set gives exactly contents t, the set of points in its leaves. Empty trees contribute no points, leaves contribute their single point, and branches combine their four subtrees. The set conversion ignores list order and repeated points. There are no additional premises.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.enumerate_member.description: The lemma states that, for any quadtree t and point p, p appears in the list enumerate t exactly when it belongs to the set contents t. Enumeration collects leaf points by concatenating the four branches’ lists, while contents combines their sets of points; both give no points for an empty tree. No additional premises are stated, and the lemma concerns membership only, without asserting an order or absence of duplicates in the list.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.enumerate_unique.description: The lemma states that if rectangle b has both side lengths equal to width d and quadtree t is valid within b at depth d, then enumerating t produces a list with no repeated points. Enumeration collects leaf points by concatenating the four child lists; validity requires each leaf point to lie in its assigned rectangle, forbids branches at depth zero, and checks children in their respective quadrant boxes at the next smaller depth. The supplied supporting lemmas state that child boxes remain square and distinct valid quadrants have disjoint enumerations, although the precise definitions of width, child boxes, and rectangle membership are not supplied.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.height.description: The recursive function height assigns a natural-number height to a qtree: Empty and Leaf nodes have height 0, while a Branch has height one greater than the largest height of its four children. Thus it counts the maximum number of branch levels along a path through the tree, recursively computing each child’s height.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.in_rect.description: The definition in_rect says that an integer-coordinate point p lies in rectangle r exactly when its first coordinate is at least xmin and strictly less than xmax, and its second coordinate is at least ymin and strictly less than ymax. Thus the lower boundaries are included and the upper boundaries are excluded; no assumption that the rectangle’s bounds are ordered is supplied.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.in_rect_dec.description: This declaration registers a global instance that decides whether a point p lies in a rectangle r: its first coordinate must be at least xmin r and strictly below xmax r, and its second coordinate must be at least ymin r and strictly below ymax r. The body unfolds this condition and invokes solve_decision to construct either a proof of membership or a proof of non-membership; the supplied input does not show the underlying coordinate types or comparison-decision instances on which this construction relies.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.insert_reference.description: insert_reference takes a depth d, a point p, and a tree t. If p lies in the domain from (0,0) to (width d,width d), including the lower boundaries and excluding the upper boundaries, it rebuilds a tree at depth d from the set of points already in t together with p; otherwise it returns t unchanged. Set union avoids duplicate points, but the supplied definitions do not establish that rebuilding preserves every point: build_tree keeps only the first point when its depth is zero, and the definitions of width, child_box, and select_points are not supplied.

This lemma states that if t is a valid quadtree at depth d within the domain from (0, 0) to (width d, width d), reference insertion of p preserves validity and gives exactly the set of points specified by insert_set. If p lies inside the domain, including its lower edges but excluding its upper edges, insertion rebuilds the tree from its existing points together with p; otherwise it leaves t unchanged. Validity requires leaves to lie in their assigned rectangles and branches to have positive remaining depth with valid children in their respective child rectangles.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.insert_set.description: insert_set takes a natural number d, an integer-coordinate point p, and a finite set of points S. It adds p to S if p lies in the square domain from (0, 0) to (width d, width d), including the lower boundaries and excluding the upper boundaries; otherwise, it returns S unchanged. Adding a point already in S leaves the set unchanged. The supplied input does not define width, so it does not establish the domain’s size for a given d.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.insertion_commut.description: The lemma states that inserting points p and q into S, using the same natural-number parameter d, gives the same result in either order. Each insertion adds its point to the set only if the point lies in domain d; otherwise it leaves the set unchanged. There are no explicit additional premises, so neither point is required to lie in the domain. The input supplies the statement but no proof.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.insertion_idempo.description: The lemma states that inserting the same point p twice into a point set S, using the same natural-number parameter d, has the same result as inserting it once. The definition adds p to S if p lies within domain d and otherwise leaves S unchanged. No additional premises are stated; the supplied input does not explain how d determines the domain.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.insertion_preser.description: The lemma states that if every point in S lies within domain d, then every point in insert_set d p S also lies within that domain. This holds because insert_set adds p only when p lies within the domain; otherwise it leaves S unchanged. The only premise is that S is admissible, so p need not already lie within the domain.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.insertion_reject.description: The lemma states that if point p lies outside the domain for natural number d, inserting p into the set S leaves S unchanged. The domain is the square from (0, 0) to (width d, width d), including its lower boundaries and excluding its upper boundaries. This follows the supplied definition of insert_set, which adds p only when p is inside that square and otherwise returns S.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.membership_repea.description: The lemma states that the pair consisting of contains_set p S and S equals itself. Here contains_set p S is the Boolean decision of whether the point p belongs to the collection S. The statement has no additional premises and expresses only reflexive equality; it does not establish any behavior of repeated membership checks.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.midx.description: The definition midx takes a natural number d and a rectangle b and returns the integer xmin b + 2^d, adding a power-of-two offset to the rectangle’s minimum x-coordinate. It imposes no conditions on the rectangle’s coordinates; despite its name, the supplied input does not establish that this value is the rectangle’s midpoint.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.midy.description: The definition midy takes a natural number d and a rectangle b and returns the integer ymin b + 2^d, adding a power-of-two offset to the rectangle’s lower y-coordinate. Despite its name, the supplied input does not establish that this value is the rectangle’s vertical midpoint, since it gives no relationship between d and the rectangle’s bounds.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.partition_points.description: The lemma states that if b is a square with side length width(S d) and every point in the list xs lies within b, then selecting points from xs in each of b’s four child rectangles and taking the union of those sets gives exactly the set of points in xs. Rectangle membership includes the lower boundaries and excludes the upper boundaries, and conversion to sets ignores duplicates and list order. The supplied input does not define width or the midpoint functions, so their precise numerical behavior is unspecified.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.point.description: The definition point names the type of pairs of integers, so a point consists of two integer values. The declaration imposes no bounds or other conditions on those values.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.points.description: The definition names `points` as the type `gset point`, where a `point` is a pair of integers. Under the usual meaning of `gset`, this represents finite sets of integer-coordinate points, though the supplied input does not define `gset` itself.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.qtree.description: The declaration defines qtree as a finite recursive tree with three forms: Empty, a Leaf containing a point (a pair of integers), or a Branch containing four subtrees named ll, lr, ul, and ur. These names suggest quadrants, but the input does not establish their spatial meaning or impose any constraints on where points belong.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.quadrant.description: The declaration defines quadrant as a type with exactly four distinct values: LL, LR, UL, and UR. Each constructor takes no arguments. The names suggest lower-left, lower-right, upper-left, and upper-right quadrants, but the supplied input does not establish that interpretation.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.quadrant_eq_dec.description: This declaration registers a global instance for deciding equality between values of quadrant, which has four constructors: LL, LR, UL, and UR. Its body uses the solve_decision tactic to construct the equality decision procedure, allowing Rocq to determine whether two quadrants are equal or unequal. The supplied input shows the declaration but does not establish that it was successfully checked.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.query_model.description: query_model takes a rectangle r and a quadtree t, collects the tree’s points into a list, and filters that list using in_rect r. Enumeration contributes no points for Empty, one point for a Leaf, and concatenates the four subtrees’ lists in order for a Branch. The exact boundary rules for rectangle membership are not supplied, so they cannot be determined from this input.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.query_model_cont.description: This lemma states that, for any rectangle r and quadtree t, converting the list returned by query_model r t into a set gives exactly the points in t’s contents that satisfy in_rect r. The contents are empty for an empty tree, a singleton for a leaf, and the union of the four children’s contents for a branch. The supplied supporting lemmas relate enumeration to tree contents and point selection to set filtering. No additional premises are stated, and the equality does not specify list order or duplicate counts.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.query_model_uniq.description: The lemma states that query_model r t contains no duplicate points if b has both side lengths equal to width d and t is valid at depth d within b. Validity allows empty trees, requires each leaf point to lie in its box, and permits branches only at positive depth, with each child valid at the next smaller depth in its corresponding child box. The query applies select_points r to the enumeration of t; the supplied enumerate_unique lemma states that this enumeration has no duplicates under the same premises. The input does not define select_points, so its precise selection behavior is unspecified.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.query_state.description: The definition query_state takes r and t and returns the pair consisting of t itself and query_model r t, which is defined by applying select_points r to enumerate t. Thus it pairs the original t with a selection computed from its enumeration; the supplied input does not establish the parameter types or the precise meanings of enumeration and selection.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.query_state_repe.description: The lemma states that applying query_state twice with the same r, passing the state returned by the first call into the second, leaves the final state equal to the original t and produces equal query results. The supplied definition returns the input state unchanged together with query_model r t, which explains both equalities. There are no explicit additional premises; the types of r and t and the meaning of query_model are not supplied.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.range_distribute.description: The lemma states that filtering the union of two point sets S and T to keep points inside a rectangle r gives the same set as filtering S and T separately and then taking their union. Here, range_set is defined using the in_rect filter, and union_set is set union. The statement applies to any rectangle r and point sets S and T, with no additional premises.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.range_empty_rect.description: The lemma states that for any rectangle r with integer bounds and any collection of points S, filtering S to points inside r gives the empty set if xmax r is at most xmin r or ymax r is at most ymin r. Membership includes the lower bounds and excludes the upper bounds, so either premise makes the corresponding coordinate condition impossible.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.range_repeated.description: The lemma states that the pair consisting of range_set r S and S equals itself. Here r is a rectangle, S is a collection of points, and range_set r S filters S using the predicate in_rect r. This is a reflexive equality with no additional premises; it asserts no further property of the filtering operation.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.range_set.description: range_set takes a rectangle r with integer bounds and a set of points S, and filters S to keep exactly the points whose x coordinate is at least xmin r and strictly less than xmax r, and whose y coordinate is at least ymin r and strictly less than ymax r. Thus the lower boundaries are included and the upper boundaries are excluded. The rectangle record imposes no requirement that the lower bounds be smaller than the upper bounds.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.range_tree_union.description: The lemma states that, if both trees t and u are valid at depth d in the domain Rect 0 0 (width d) (width d), querying their reference union with r returns exactly the union of the sets returned by querying each tree separately. The reference union is built from the union of their contents; validity requires leaves to lie in their assigned rectangles and branches to respect the remaining depth and child rectangles. Results are compared as sets, so order and duplicates do not matter. The precise geometric meaning of r is not supplied.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.rectangle.description: The declaration defines a record type called rectangle, constructed with Rect, containing four integer (Z) fields: xmin, ymin, xmax, and ymax. Their names suggest minimum and maximum coordinates, but the declaration imposes no ordering constraints or other conditions ensuring that they describe a valid rectangle.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.reference_insert.description: This lemma states that, if t is valid at depth d within the square domain from (0,0) to (width d,width d), inserting points p and q in either order produces the same set of stored points, though not necessarily identical tree structures. Validity requires leaves to lie in their assigned rectangles and branches to have positive remaining depth with valid children in their respective child boxes. Reference insertion rebuilds the tree with the added point when it lies inside the domain and otherwise leaves the tree unchanged, so neither point needs an additional inside-domain premise.

The lemma states that, if t is a valid quadtree at depth d within domain d, inserting the same point p twice with insert_reference gives the same set of stored points as inserting it once; it does not assert that the resulting tree structures are identical. Validity requires leaves to lie within their assigned rectangles and branches to have positive remaining depth with valid children. Reference insertion rebuilds the tree from its existing points plus p when p lies inside the domain, and otherwise leaves it unchanged.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.root_square.description: The lemma states that for every natural number d, domain d satisfies square d: its maximum x-coordinate equals its minimum x-coordinate plus width d, and likewise for its y-coordinates. The domain is defined as Rect 0 0 (width d) (width d). There are no additional premises, but the supplied input does not define Rect or the coordinate accessors, so their interpretation is not fully established.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.route.description: The definition route selects a quadrant for an integer-coordinate point p by comparing its x and y coordinates with xmin b + width d and ymin b + width d: it returns LL when both coordinates are below their thresholds, UL when only x is below, LR when only y is below, and UR when neither is below. Equality follows the same branch as being above the threshold. It does not require the point to lie inside b or check the rectangle’s bounds; because width is not defined in the input, the geometric meaning of these thresholds is uncertain.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.select_points.description: select_points is intended to keep the points in xs that lie within rectangle r: each point is a pair of integers, and its coordinates must be at least the rectangle’s minimum bounds and strictly below its maximum bounds. No assumption that the minimum bounds are below the maximum bounds is stated. The definition of filter is not supplied, so how it uses the proposition-valued in_rect predicate is unclear.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.select_points_me.description: The lemma states that a point p belongs to select_points r xs exactly when it belongs to the original list xs and lies inside rectangle r. Being inside means its x and y coordinates are each at least the corresponding minimum and strictly below the corresponding maximum, so lower boundaries are included and upper boundaries are excluded. The supplied definition describes select_points as filtering xs by this condition; no additional premises are stated.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.select_points_se.description: The lemma states that, for any rectangle r and list of points xs, filtering the list to points satisfying in_rect r and then converting it to a set gives the same set as first converting the list to a set and then applying the same filter. Set conversion discards duplicates and order, and no additional premises are stated. The input does not define the precise boundary convention used by in_rect.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.square.description: The definition square d b states that the rectangle b, whose coordinates are integers, has both its horizontal and vertical extent equal to 2 raised to the natural-number power d: xmax is xmin plus 2^d, and ymax is ymin plus 2^d. It defines a proposition about b rather than constructing a rectangle or proving that any particular rectangle satisfies it.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.subdivision_cove.description: The lemma states that if rectangle b has both side lengths equal to width(S d), then a point p lies in b exactly when it lies in at least one of the four child rectangles formed using midx d b and midy d b. Rectangle membership includes the lower boundaries and excludes the upper boundaries. The supplied child_route and child_subset lemmas state the two directions of this equivalence; the definitions of width and the split coordinates are not supplied, so their precise numerical meaning is unspecified.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.subdivision_disj.description: The lemma states that two distinct child quadrants of the same rectangle are disjoint: if k differs from j and point p lies in child_box d b k, then p does not lie in child_box d b j. These child boxes use the rectangle’s bounds and the midpoint functions at parameter d; membership includes the lower bounds and excludes the upper bounds on both coordinates. The supplied declaration states this property but does not include its proof.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.union_reference.description: union_reference d t u constructs a quadtree by taking the set union of the points contained in t and u, converting that set to a list with elements, and passing it to build_tree with depth d and the rectangle Rect 0 0 (width d) (width d). The builder returns Empty for an empty list, a leaf for a single point, and otherwise recursively builds four children while decreasing the depth; at depth zero it keeps only the first point. No assumptions or correctness guarantee are stated, so the input does not establish that the resulting tree preserves every point in the union; elements, width, and the child-selection helpers are not defined here.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.union_reference_.description: The lemma states that if both quadtrees t and u are valid at depth d within the domain from (0, 0) to (width d, width d), then union_reference d t u, which rebuilds a tree from the union of their point sets, is also valid there and contains exactly the points present in either input. Validity requires leaves to lie within their assigned rectangles and branches to respect the depth limit and recursively satisfy validity in their child rectangles.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.union_set.description: The definition union_set takes two sets of points, S and T, and returns their union: the set containing every point that belongs to either S or T. The supplied dependency defines points as gset point; this declaration introduces no additional premises or correctness claims.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.unit_unique.description: The lemma states that any two points p and q inside a rectangle b satisfying square 0 b must be equal. The supplied definitions and width_zero make b have width and height 1, with membership including the lower boundaries and excluding the upper boundaries. The coordinate types are not supplied, so the input does not establish why such a rectangle can contain at most one point.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.valid.description: valid defines when a quadtree fits a rectangle within a given depth: an empty tree is always valid, and a leaf is valid when its point lies inside the rectangle, including the lower bounds but excluding the upper bounds. A branch is invalid at depth zero; at depth d + 1, all four children must be valid at depth d in their respective lower-left, lower-right, upper-left, and upper-right boxes. Those boxes use midx and midy at depth d, whose definitions are not supplied, so their exact split positions are unknown. The definition recurses structurally on the tree.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.valid_contents.description: The lemma states that if rectangle b has width and height width d and quadtree t is valid at depth d within b, then every point in t’s contents lies inside b, including its lower boundaries and excluding its upper boundaries. Contents collects all leaf points; validity allows empty trees, requires leaf points to lie in their assigned rectangle, and requires branches to have positive remaining depth with each subtree valid in its corresponding child rectangle.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.valid_height.description: The lemma states that if a quadtree t is valid within rectangle b at depth d, its height is at most d. Height is zero for empty trees and leaves, and one plus the maximum child height for branches. Validity allows empty trees, requires leaf points to lie in their rectangle, and permits branches only at positive depth, with all four children valid at depth one less in their corresponding child boxes. The supplied input states the lemma but does not include its proof.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.width.description: The definition width takes a natural number d and returns the integer 2 raised to the power d, converting d to an integer with Z.of_nat before exponentiation.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.width_bound.description: The lemma states that for any natural number d at most 30, width d is at most 1,073,741,824 (2^30). Here width d is defined as the integer 2 raised to the power d, so the premise bounds the exponent and the conclusion bounds the resulting width.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.width_positive.description: The lemma states that width d is strictly positive for every natural number d. Here, width d is defined as the integer 2 raised to the power d, with d converted from a natural number to an integer. There are no additional premises in the supplied declaration; no proof is supplied.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.width_succ.description: The lemma states that increasing a natural-number depth d by one doubles its width: width (S d) = 2 × width d. Here S d means d + 1, and width d is defined as the integer 2 raised to the power d. There are no additional premises.

cjr.quadtree.spec.model.width_zero.description: The lemma states that width at depth zero is 1. The supplied definition makes width at a natural-number depth d the integer 2 raised to d, so this is the zero-exponent case, 2⁰ = 1. The statement has no additional premises; no proof is supplied.
